title: FlashInfer paged decode: freeze backend selection and graph buffers
summary: Paged attention separates planning from execution; auto dispatch and CUDA graph buffer ownership are part of the reproducibility boundary.

hardware: NVIDIA CUDA; the inspected auto-cuDNN dispatch specifically distinguishes SM100/SM103 and frontend versions
software: flashinfer-ai/flashinfer at 3637083a3a3d08538cce60937cd876b17779c6f0; later revisions need reinspection
conditions: Paged KV decode with known head dimensions, dtype, page layout and batch shape
Caller-owned graph buffers must remain valid across planning and replay

claims.description: BatchDecodeWithPagedKVCacheWrapper exposes resolved_backend after planning. Auto selection depends on architecture, kernel availability, shapes and optional cuDNN/CuTe dependencies.

The inspected cuDNN path accepts a narrower feature set than the whole library; it excludes RoPE, soft-cap and FP8/NVFP4 KV. Captured block tables and backend choice cannot change arbitrarily between re-plans.

downstream_impact: vLLM: record the resolved attention backend and dependency tuple when comparing upgrades; an unchanged backend=auto argument does not freeze the implementation.
vLLM-Omni: transfer the dispatch/buffer-ownership checks only to adapters actually calling these APIs; this LLM decode card does not establish diffusion attention support.
vllm-ascend: the CUDA kernels are not portable; only the explicit-dispatch and lifetime checks are candidate review practices.
recommendations: Treat downstream impact as an InferRSI transfer hypothesis, not an upstream compatibility or performance result.
validation_plan: Compare numerical outputs with a reference over supported dtype/head/layout/masking combinations and require a defined fallback for unsupported inputs.
Measure cold planning/JIT, warm run, graph capture and replay separately; vary batch and sequence shapes and test caller-owned buffer reuse.
limitations: The library GPU table is not an operator-by-operator support matrix.
No downstream dependency bump or universal speedup is recommended from this snapshot.
Point-in-time source extraction, not a historical commit-delta audit. No local accelerator or model-quality reproduction was run.
